comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C73-C76 regarding transport assays. Both evaluations find the data on Nup153's dual effects on passive and active transport to be well-supported. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, peer reviewer also rates as SUPPORTED with no specific concerns raised.

Both address the overall model (C10, C105, C109-C110, C112-C113) of imp-β•Nup153 meshwork at the nuclear face. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED noting appropriate presentation as a model. Peer reviewer also rates as SUPPORTED, calling it 'new interesting insights,' though Reviewer 1 raises minor terminological concerns about comparing to FG gels.

Strong agreement on claims C77-C85 regarding permeability barrier. Both evaluations find the evidence for imp-β•Nup153-dependent steric barrier well-supported. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on convergence of observations. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, affirming the manuscript 'provides proof that RanGTP influences the permeability of the NPC itself.'

Both address in vitro complex formation (C90-C97). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on convergence of multiple approaches. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning the motivation and logic, noting the result is unsurprising, and requesting additional controls including testing Ran's effect on TRN1•Nup153FG complexes.

Both address photobleach counting data (C69-C72, C117). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the quantitative analysis and statistical methods appropriate. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, expressing serious methodological concerns about stepwise bleaching analysis, stating 'the true number of Imp-beta at the pore might easily be several folds off' and requesting improved data presentation.

Both address the functional component interpretation (C5, C88, C118). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on convergence of kinetic and functional evidence. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, endorsing that the manuscript 'provides proof that RanGTP influences the permeability of the NPC itself' with no challenges to this interpretation.

Both address dSTORM localization data (C49-C56, C61-C67) showing spatial reorganization. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on spatial precision and consistency. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, raising substantial concerns about data presentation, normalization, and potential technical artifacts, requesting raw data and clarification of methods.

Both address heterogeneity observations (C63, C123-C124). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting the observation is well-documented though biological significance unclear. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED with no concerns raised about the heterogeneity observations.

Both address TRN1 comparison data (C98-C100, C103). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the functional distinction well-supported by current data and literature. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting an experiment testing Ran's effect on TRN1•Nup153FG complexes and questioning how the generic mechanism rationalizes the different in vivo behaviors.

Both address confocal microscopy observations (C31-C34) of rim accumulation and RanGTP effects. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the observations straightforward and well-documented. Peer reviewer rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly requesting 'raw data for the Imp-YFP experiment that is a part of Figure 1,' indicating concern about data presentation.

Both address FRAP data and two-pool model (C35-C37, C43-C45). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on convergence of FRAP and photo-conversion data. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, stating 'it is good to see that two different methods (FRAP, and photoconversion based FLAP) support their conclusion.'

Both address photo-conversion data (C39-C42) showing stable pool. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED as part of convergent evidence for two pools. Peer reviewer rates as SUPPORTED, explicitly endorsing photo-conversion data as corroborating evidence for the two-pool model.

Partial overlap on dSTORM observations (C46-C48). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the imaging results straightforward with appropriate acknowledgment of limitations. Peer reviewer's UNCERTAIN rating for R4 addresses broader concerns about Figure 3 data including these claims, questioning normalization and requesting raw data.

OpenEval addresses claims C121-C122 regarding inferences about Ran-insensitive pool location from dSTORM and counting data, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses claims C86-C87 regarding passive equilibration observations and RanGTP wash experiments, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.

OpenEval addresses claim C116 comparing FRAP data with Rabut et al. 2004 to validate the experimental system, rating as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this validation claim.

OpenEval addresses claims C125-C127 regarding speculative proposals about cellular regulation of RanGTP gradient, rating as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental evidence. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative claims.

OpenEval addresses claims C128-C129 regarding future applications of the in vitro system, rating as UNCERTAIN as these cannot be evaluated based on current data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these forward-looking claims.
